clue.text: Maybe Jack's married with a second taken in this is quite spicy

indicators.note: taken in says the pair of pieces after 'with' is held inside the first pair

parts.note: a jack is one example of a playing card
taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a newly-wed Jack, joined by a second person, makes things quite spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks Jack as one example of a playing card; 'taken in' signals the container, and 'a second' is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic spice from India, so it is a pod that is quite spicy.

clue.text: Samoa and New Zealand's wild warlike women

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the island name and the country code run riot

parts.note: NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand

explanation.surface: Women of the Pacific islands are pictured as fierce warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SAMOA with NZ.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Amazons were a nation of female warriors.

clue.text: Grounds for limb's length being cut under the doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this piece is written below the doctor

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: being cut says a letter is cut away from the limbs

parts.note: legs are limbs

explanation.surface: A doctor amputates a limb, losing some of its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like reasons, but it means coffee sediment. 'being cut' signals the deletion; 'under' places the trimmed limbs below the doctor in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs and grounds are both the sediment left at the bottom of a coffee cup or wine glass.

clue.text: Hooch is soon distilled and initially hidden in tunnel

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters sit within the word for a tunnel

parts.note: a mine is a tunnel dug underground

indicators.note: distilled suggests the letters of soon are processed into a new form
initially picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Illicit liquor is quickly distilled and hidden in an underground tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distilled' is the anagram signal, fitting the liquor surface; 'initially' picks one letter; 'in' puts the result inside the tunnel word.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled spirit, the same rough liquor called hooch.

clue.text: There's more happiness in barking-when it's up the wrong tree?

definitions.text: when it's up the wrong tree?

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the three words are rearranged crazily

explanation.surface: A dog barking up the wrong tree is said to be happier for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' rearranges MORE HAPPINESS IN; the definition borrows the idiom 'barking up the wrong tree', being mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking up the wrong tree is being mistaken, so the state is a misunderstanding.

clue.text: Urchin's leader of gang — better to do this?

parts.note: a gamin is a street urchin

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of gang

explanation.surface: A street kid heads a gang, wondering whether it is better to do this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not 'more good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gambling is what a punter who places bets does.

clue.text: A bit of wind's nothing to relish

parts.note: a gust is a brief rush of wind
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A breath of wind offers nothing to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, the same as relish.

clue.text: Prig is in alarm with us playing possum perhaps?

indicators.note: is in says the short word for a prig is placed inside the rearranged letters
playing suggests the letters of alarm and us are toyed with

parts.note: PI, short for pious, describes a sanctimonious prig

explanation.surface: A prude is alarmed when we start playing possum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prig' is a sanctimonious person, given by the abbreviation for pious. 'playing' signals the anagram and 'is in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is an Australian pouched animal, one example of the pouched group.

clue.text: At this time and place, out of the running

parts.note: now means at this time
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Someone declares the present time and place out of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who finishes nowhere is out of the placings, not in contention.

clue.text: Fleet mounts strike across here

indicators.note: strike suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Workers strike right across this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' rearranges ACROSS HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorses are swift animals that people ride, so fleet mounts.

clue.text: Scraps boat journeys

definitions.meaning: scraps as a verb meaning quarrels or squabbles

explanation.surface: Leftovers are carried on trips by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows are noisy quarrels; rows are also outings in a rowing boat.

clue.text: Expenses accommodating first class in cruises

indicators.note: accommodating means housing the grade inside the word for expenses

parts.note: costs are expenses
A is a first-class grade

explanation.surface: First-class cabins push up the expenses of sea cruises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts A inside COSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to glide along without effort, as a car cruises.

clue.text: Pimp in favour of right to have fix?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
cure means fix, remedy

explanation.surface: A pimp is backed for having the right to fix things.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurer is one who obtains prostitutes for clients, a pimp.

clue.text: Trained fruit tree to stretch between pears up the wall

indicators.note: between places the word for stretching out within the jumbled fruit
up the wall means crazy, so the letters of pears go wild

parts.note: to lie is to stretch out flat

explanation.surface: A gardener trains a pear tree against the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the wall' means mad, so it is the anagram signal, though it fits the trained tree's wall; 'between' puts the stretching word inside the jumbled fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall or frame.

clue.text: Insectivores like going round edges of nest and a tree that's rotten

indicators.note: going round says the word for like surrounds everything that follows

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of nest
rotten suggests the letters of a tree have decayed into a new order

explanation.surface: Insect-eating animals circle a nest in a rotten tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges of' picks two letters, 'that's rotten' is the anagram signal, and 'going round' wraps the word for like around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Anteaters feed on ants and termites, so they are insect eaters.

clue.text: Happened to pine away from Parisienne

indicators.note: away from means the letters of pine are removed from the Paris word

explanation.surface: A homesick Parisian woman pines away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' takes P, I, N, E, in that order, out of PARISIENNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has arisen has come about, happened.

clue.text: I sat in car with map out — it should see you home

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: sat in says the single letter is seated within the word for map out

parts.note: to plot is to map out

explanation.surface: A driver sits in the car with the map, trusting it to get home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sat in' puts I inside PLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot steers a craft automatically, so it should bring you back without effort.

clue.text: She's wrapped up with a temperature and a bandage

indicators.note: wrapped up means the word she encloses the other letters

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A feverish patient is wrapped up and bandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped up' puts W, A, T inside SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap or bind with cloth, as one does a bandage.

clue.text: Article included in Sport might provide forecast

indicators.note: included in says the article sits within the word for sport

parts.note: to sport a hat is to wear it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A sports report might come with a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is the verb, to wear something showily, not athletics; 'included in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists forecast the climate conditions of the coming days.

clue.text: Can't stand around cooking pot left in top of oven

indicators.note: around says the word for can't stand surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to hate something is not to be able to stand it

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of pot are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook cannot bear a pot left on top of the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' is the anagram signal, fitting the kitchen surface; 'around' wraps the word for can't stand around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotplate is a heated ring on a cooker's top surface.

clue.text: The big picture?

parts.note: a film that was a huge blockbuster, named for an enormous ship

explanation.definitionFit: Titanic was a hugely successful 1997 film, and titanic means gigantic.

clue.text: Unsteadiness, though not ill we need a holiday

indicators.note: not says the word for sick is removed from the word for wavering

parts.note: vacillation is wavering, unsteadiness
ill is sick

explanation.surface: Feeling wobbly though not ill, we decide we need a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes ILL out of VACILLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacation is a break from work, a holiday.

clue.text: Lump of metal making other clasps

indicators.note: clasps means the words grip the answer within them

explanation.surface: Making some other metal object to hold clasps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clasps' holds the answer inside 'makING OTher'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast block of metal, usually gold or silver.

clue.text: Very quick interval between beginning and end of panto

indicators.note: between says the break sits within the outer letters of panto
beginning and end of picks the first and last letters of panto

parts.note: a rest is an interval or break

explanation.surface: A pantomime has an interval between its opening and ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning and end of' gives P and O; 'between' puts REST inside. A panto is a British Christmas family stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo.

clue.text: Supplement might be tax free with no frills

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged
with no frills strips the first and last letters of free

explanation.surface: A supplement could be tax-free if it comes without frills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no frills' trims FREE to RE; 'might be' rearranges TAX + RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional item, a supplement.

clue.text: Maybe trainer's push to pull out victory?

indicators.note: to pull out means a letter is withdrawn from the word for push

parts.note: to shove is to push

explanation.surface: A coach pushes a team to snatch victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trainer' is a sports shoe, not a coach; 'to pull out' takes V from SHOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a kind of sports footwear.

clue.text: Heads off here when remorse in evidence finally? Look into it

indicators.note: into says the word for look is put inside the rest

parts.note: guilt is remorse
lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of evidence

explanation.surface: A guilty person faces the evidence at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks the last letter of evidence; 'into' tells you the archaic exclamation goes inside everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillotine was the French beheading machine, where heads came off.

clue.text: Tripos after revision? Good luck to you!

indicators.note: after revision says the letters of Tripos are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A student revising for Cambridge's Tripos exams is wished good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revision' rearranges TRIPOS, the name for Cambridge University's final honours exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German toast wishing good health and luck.

clue.text: Creeping bird, name unknown, on a layer of straw

parts.note: NU is the abbreviation for name unknown
thatch is a roof covering of straw

explanation.surface: An unnamed bird sits on a thatched roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeping' describes how the bird climbs tree trunks.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small bird that creeps up and down tree trunks.
